title: Exact Sine of an obtuse Standard Angle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Using a reference angle, evaluate $\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ exactly and justify its sign.

steps.title: Identify the Quadrant
steps.explanation: The angle lies between $\pi/2$ and $\pi$, so its terminal side is in the second quadrant.
steps.why: Quadrant membership determines whether the trig value is positive or negative.

steps.title: Compute the Reference Angle
steps.explanation: The acute angle made with the $x$-axis is $\pi/3$, so the magnitude equals $\sin(\pi/3)=\sqrt{3}/2$.
steps.why: Reference angles reduce any standard angle to a memorized special value.

steps.title: Apply the Quadrant Sign
steps.explanation: Sine is the $y$-coordinate, which stays positive in Quadrant II, so the value keeps the plus sign.
steps.why: ASTC sign rules: only sine (and cosecant) are positive in the second quadrant.
